### [An opinionated guide to which AI to use to do stuff](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Jul/27/an-opinionated-guide-to-which-ai-to-use-to-do-stuff/#atom-everything)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-07-27

Ethan Mollick's AI guide now emphasizes agentic systems capable of extensive human-equivalent work, with a focus on AI access to user computers via modes like ChatGPT Work/Codex and Claude Cowork/Code, while Gemini has fallen off his list.

- Ethan Mollick's AI guide shifted from chat-focused models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) to agentic systems that perform "many hours of real human work in one go."
- Gemini is no longer on Mollick's list due to Google's lack of an established entry in the Codex/ChatGPT Work/Cowork category.
- AI companies provide computer access modes: ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork for their platforms, and ChatGPT Work/Codex and Claude Cowork/Code for desktop apps with more features.
- ChatGPT mobile's "Work" mode enables its Code Interpreter container to access the internet, unlike its default "Chat" mode.
- The naming conventions for AI agent modes (e.g., ChatGPT Work vs. Codex, Claude Cowork vs. Code) are inconsistent and confusing.

**Why it matters:** The evolution towards agentic AI systems with direct computer access significantly expands AI capabilities for complex tasks, but inconsistent naming conventions create user confusion.
